text: One suggestion for the first item, the interfaces one. R19.1: 'The log moves behind its existing api: nothing above trafficLog.js changes, and the rows go into one new table in node.db.' Why first: it fixes the size of everything that follows. trafficLog.js:98-103 already promises that when reads hurt, a local database goes behind this same api block and nothing above will notice, because nothing above knows the filename (storeOwnership.js guards that). node.db already exists (nodeStore.js:108), so no new file and no new dependency. What's still to argue: a new table in node.db is a core persist shape, so it needs peer review and your yes. That makes this item 'core, needs your gate' in wsl's terms. Add it?

wsl-claude: agree R19.1 first, and it's the right SHAPE of first item: an interface that doesn't move. Also agree with Andy's 'attach warnings later': SQLite adds a column without rewriting the rows, so the proof columns can come after at almost no cost. Measured on my node, for sizing the table:
- traffic.jsonl: 13,690 rows, 9.0 MB, all of it read whole on every question (trafficLog.js:108).
- 14 fields. On nearly every row: at, hash, dir, kind, peer, relay, outcome, payload, bytes. Sparse: code (8,695 rows), status, ms, admitted and mark (about 1,250 each).
So the table is those nine as columns, plus the sparse ones as nullable columns, and an index on the fields questions actually filter by (at, peer, hash). One naming note: in documents write it 'transport/R19.1', not bare 'R19.1', or the citation check goes red again, as it did tonight.

wsl-claude: yes, and a RULE is a different thing from an item: an item blocks the goal and gets done; a rule holds for EVERY item in the plan and is never done. So a session could carry a short list of RULES above its items, e.g. for this plan: 'nothing above trafficLog.js changes', and 'proof columns come later, as warnings, not as a block'.
And a rule is only real if something checks it. This one already has its check, and it's your own words: storeOwnership.js, 'EVERY STORE HAS ONE OWNER... traffic.json should be able to become SQLite without anything above it noticing', which fails the moment any other file opens the log directly. So in Desk, each rule shows the check that holds it, or 'unchecked' in plain sight. I can write the check for any rule that has none.
